newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan LDP reform plan fails to support stocks.
newsitem.headline: Japan LDP reform plan fails to support stocks.

text.p: The Japanese stock market showed only muted reaction on Thursday to a plan by the ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) to speed up the government's "Big Bang" financial market reforms.
Brokers said the plan, including the scrapping of securities transaction taxes, failed to impress the market as it had already been discounted to some extent.
News that the LDP was considering abolishing the tax had boosted the sagging stock market earlier this year as it is likely to enliven stock trading.
"The possibility of the tax abolition has been reported (by the media) repeatedly, and the market took it for granted," said one broker at a Japanese securities house.
Other brokers said deregulation was not wholly good news for the stock market. "We can't simply be happy about it," said Harushige Kobayashi, deputy general manager at Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd.
Deregulation often creates fierce competition among brokerages, which hurts the stock market initially, brokers said.
The Nikkei 225 average fell by more than one percent on Thursday, dragged down by futures selling.
According to a draft report obtained by Reuters, the LDP's administrative reform panel is calling for the abolition of the taxes from the start of fiscal 1998/99.
An LDP source told Reuters on Thursday that the ruling party is seeking to work out a deregulation plan as the government is scheduled to finalise Japan's deregulation programme by the end of March.

Last November, Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto unveiled a five-year plan to liberalise Japan's financial markets by 2001 and catch up with reforms carried out more than a decade ago in Europe and North America.
